Welcome

Central Desert Regional Council acknowledges the traditional owners and custodians of the lands on which we work.
We pay our respects to their Elders past and present.

Transcript
Welcome to Central Desert Regional Council.
I'm Adrian Dixon, the president of the council. I'm excited to introduce you to our website.
Our website is a great resource for information about our council, our communities, and the service we provide.
Our communities include Lajamanu, Willowra, Nyirripi, Yuendumu, Yuelamu, Laramba, Anmatjere, Engawala and Atitjere.
These communities are home to over 4000 people who come from a variety of Aboriginal languages. They are rich in culture, history, and have their own unique stories to tell.
The Central Desert region is a vast and beautiful area covering over 282,000 square kilometres.
It is home to a variety of wildlife, including kangaroos, emus, dingoes.
The region is also home to many cultural sites, including art, rock art and sacred places.
I encourage you to explore our website and learn more about our council and the work we do.
We're here to serve you. We want to make sure you have the information you need to get involved in our communities.
Thank you for visiting our website.

Welcome

Central Desert Regional Council acknowledges the traditional owners and custodians of the lands on which we work.
We pay our respects to their Elders past and present.

Transcript
Welcome to Central Desert Regional Council.
I'm Adrian Dixon, the president of the council. I'm excited to introduce you to our website.
Our website is a great resource for information about our council, our communities, and the service we provide.
Our communities include Lajamanu, Willowra, Nyirripi, Yuendumu, Yuelamu, Laramba, Anmatjere, Engawala and Atitjere.
These communities are home to over 4000 people who come from a variety of Aboriginal languages. They are rich in culture, history, and have their own unique stories to tell.
The Central Desert region is a vast and beautiful area covering over 282,000 square kilometres.
It is home to a variety of wildlife, including kangaroos, emus, dingoes.
The region is also home to many cultural sites, including art, rock art and sacred places.
I encourage you to explore our website and learn more about our council and the work we do.
We're here to serve you. We want to make sure you have the information you need to get involved in our communities.
Thank you for visiting our website.
